A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Adversarial Flow Models with the same authors, implemented framework, and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-256 generation results, hyperparameter and architecture experiments, qualitative analyses, and one-dimensional transport simulations.

after.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet-256 results, one-dimensional transport experiments, OT-decay ablations, and gradient-normalization diagnostics.

M1.justification: The implemented losses, architectures, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. However, v2 removes the optional multi-step guidance extension in v1 Appendix D, Equation (36), which projected generated samples onto another flow using an additionally time-conditioned classifier. This narrows the proposed variants without establishing a change to the evaluated method.

E1.justification: ImageNet-256 and the principal Gaussian-to-mixture toy experiments remain. v2 removes v1 Appendix F's separate scenario transporting between distributions that are both multimodal Gaussian mixtures, reducing coverage of alternative source-distribution conditions.

E2.justification: Tables 4–9 retain the same benchmark comparators, including AlphaFlow, TiM, and GAT. Outside those tables, v2 removes v1 Appendix C.1's reported exploration of a Lipschitz-constrained discriminator using spectral normalization and L2 attention; the corresponding WGAN discussion no longer reports that tested alternative.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds an OT schedule decaying from 0.2 to zero over 100 epochs for B/2 1NFE. Appendix G adds a with/without-normalization control measuring separate gradient norms during training. The retained ImageNet preprocessing, class-balanced 50k evaluation, model configurations, and Table 11 training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds the zero-terminal-OT ablation and gradient-normalization diagnostics in Figures 14–15. It removes the multimodal transport case study from v1 Figure 14 and qualitative negative findings about Lipschitz-constrained and dropout-based discriminator variants. The principal guidance, depth, and qualitative image analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 newly reports consistent toy-model mappings across different random initializations, without specifying their number or establishing additional runs. Table 1 retains its two-run averages and variation reporting; no new confidence intervals or significance tests are supplied.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds FID 8.69 for decay to zero, alongside the retained 8.51 for decay to 0.01. New gradient traces and initialization-consistency findings are reported, while the multimodal transport and some exploratory discriminator findings disappear. The benchmark results in Tables 4–9, including headline FIDs 2.38, 2.08, and 1.94, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 replace the asserted equivalence to flow matching's Wasserstein-optimal transport with a Brenier-based uniqueness argument, specifying absolute continuity and quadratic cost. v2 also introduces idealized capacity/optimization assumptions and acknowledges that the combined losses need not enforce exact marginal matching in practice. v1 Appendix E's extended flow-matching/DDPM derivations are removed.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the assertion that the generator learns the same optimal transport as flow matching and instead says it is encouraged to learn a deterministic mapping. This materially qualifies a central theoretical claim. The principal generation, training-stability, ImageNet-performance, and deep-model contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.6 substantially reframes generalization, adding a JS-versus-forward-KL and outlier-sensitivity explanation as a hypothesis. Appendix G newly says gradient normalization is not strictly necessary for best performance. v2 explicitly limits the work to discrete-time modeling and training from scratch, while removing detailed vanishing-gradient discussions and the objection about DINO-derived prior knowledge.

D1.justification: The abstract newly provides a code-availability statement and repository link. The implementation listings and architecture/hyperparameter schedules in Tables 10–11 are retained. The PDFs establish this added access disclosure, not the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds Align Your Flow (AYF) to the continuous-time flow-map discussion, without evaluating it as a baseline. It prunes references and discussion concerning diffusion bridges, perceptual guidance, and image/video foundation models. The main positioning against GAN and consistency methods remains.

P1.justification: Prose is extensively rewritten throughout, with transport-map terminology and AF-to-AFM renaming. Guidance and generalization sections are reordered, training techniques move from Section 3.9 to Appendix C, and the appendices are reorganized. v2 also introduces a dedicated limitations/future-work subsection and an impact statement.

P2.justification: The two-column design and most visual content remain. v2 adds running headers, moves table captions above tables, and relocates several floats. Table 2 gains a row, while the old multimodal Figure 14 is removed and two gradient-trace figures are added as Figures 14–15.

improvement.justification: v2 better qualifies the central transport claim by stating assumptions and acknowledging the practical competition between OT regularization and distribution matching. The added OT control, gradient diagnostics, and code pointer improve transparency while preserving the main empirical evidence. Losing the multimodal example and some negative-result detail is a tradeoff; the supported net gain is limited.
